newsitem.title: USA: Snooping photographer, private eye get jail time.
newsitem.headline: Snooping photographer, private eye get jail time.

text.p: A photographer and a private detective were ordered on Wednesday to spend six months in jail for tapping the telephone of a girlfriend of the future king of Spain.

Photographer Carlos Arriazu Sanchez and Carlos Fernandez, a Miami, Florida-based private detective, were convicted in August after a two-week trial of eavesdropping on Giselle (Gigi) Howard, a 26-year-old former model whose romance with Prince Felipe of Spain made headlines in Europe last year.

"The motive was greed, pure and simple," said Manhattan Supreme Court Judge Franklin Weissberg. "Had they not been discovered, (they) would have stolen her most intimate secrets and caused them to become published internationally."

Arriazu created a sensation last year when he snapped pictures of Howard and the 28-year-old prince frolicking at a St. Martin beachfront in the Caribbean. The photos appeared in several publications in Spain, Italy, France and Britain.
Both men had faced a maximum of one-and-a-half to four years in prison. Their lawyers urged they get probation and community service.
Fernandez asked for leniency, saying loss of his investigator's license was a severe punishment.
"The conviction will forever deprive me of a living," he said, adding that his business was in shambles and he was near bankruptcy.
Through an interpreter, Arriazu said, "I am sorry for what has occurred. I'm never going to do it again."
